rival_explanations: It is a numerosity detector that treats spelled-out number words and digit tokens alike, so ' fifteen' and ' seven' would fire nearly as strongly as their digit counterparts.

It is a citation-and-decimal detector rather than a context-free one: it fires on the tail of multi-digit tokens only when they follow punctuation in references, decimals or dates, and stays quiet on numbers inside ordinary prose such as '15 dollars' or '7 days'.
It fires on any token containing a digit character, so alphanumeric tokens such as 'H2O', 'mp3' or 'COVID-19' would also peak as strongly as pure-digit tokens.
